svg.title: 2. Wolbachia field evidence: three distinct observation streams
svg.desc: Release containers produce mosquitoes and supply stage-aware QA observations. Adult monitoring traps supply specimens for species identification and laboratory infection assays. Dengue surveillance supplies clinical outcomes for a separate epidemiological design. None of these measurements substitutes for another.

g.text: Three observation streams with different questions and reference methods.

g.title: Laboratory Wolbachia stock Reference field programme [1, 2]
Mosquito release container (MRC) Eggs > larvae > pupae > adults Releases mosquitoes; not a capture trap
Stage-aware container QA Counts / condition / dates Separate emergence or outcome assessment
Adult mosquito monitoring BG-Sentinel trap example [1, 2]
Species identification + lab assay PCR / qPCR or other validated method Infection is not read from a photograph
Wolbachia prevalence Positive specimens / specimens tested Retain sample, place and date
Dengue surveillance Dated, located health records [3]
Case definition and reporting Laboratory confirmation where required Population / intervention context
Epidemiological impact evaluation Comparator, study design, uncertainty Distinct from a container-count trend

g.text: Reference field workflows [1–3], not a rearing or release protocol. See the README references.
Fewer visible larvae alone do not establish successful adult emergence or reduced dengue.
